newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Fierce competition forces Brazil insurers to merge.
newsitem.headline: Fierce competition forces Brazil insurers to merge.

text.p: Mergers and acquisitions are booming among Brazilian insurers as the market grows and becomes more competitive due to low inflation and ongoing social security reforms, analysts said.

Roberto Westenberger of Tillinghast Modelo, a unit of Towers Perrin group, said merged firms are offering more sophisticated products and upgrading technology to capture larger slices of the promising pensions and life and health insurance sectors.

Analysts said 11 mergers and acquisitions were reported in the sector in the first quarter, up 175 percent from four in the same period last year, continuing a trend begun after the government imposed its Real anti-inflation plan in mid-1994.
In 1993, one merger was reported in Brazil's insurance sector. Last year, M&As totalled 16.
That was because a lack of competition left Brazil's insurance market tiny and dominated by only a few local firms, said Jose Alonso, a consultant at KPMG Peat Marwick in Brazil.

Although the industry's future profile remains nebulous, analysts believe the wave of M&As coupled with the opening of the economy and social security reforms will boost competition nationwide, he said.
Analysts said the trend will lead to the creation of regional insurers to serve specific states and small insurance companies focused on specialized market niches.

They also said the market's future performance still depends on regulations for the opening of the country's reinsurance industry and breaking up of the state's monopoly on insuring companies against work-related accidents.

Analysts pointed out three types of M&As in the country's insurance sector. First, foreign insurers with operations in Brazil, mostly European, are raising investments in the country by increasing their stakes in Brazilian firms.
Second, foreign insurers with no operations in Brazil are forming joint-ventures with local insurance firms struggling to compete in the local market.
"In this second type of M&As there are many U.S. insurance firms like ITT Hartford (Group Inc ), which formed a joint-venture with Brazilian insurer Icatu Seguros," said KPMG's Alonso.
The third type of M&A is the acquisition of small local firms by big and medium-sized local companies looking to expand their customer base, Alonso said.
